chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from 'Uthman from Ibn Abi Ya'fur from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a Muslim slave man, is his testimony accepted for those other than his masters? He said: 'It is accepted for debts and small matters.'
ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of a Muslim slave valid in court according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates the scope of a Muslim slave's testimony (*shahada*) for non-masters, restricting its validity to debts and minor financial transactions. This ruling reflects the classical juristic consideration of a slave's limited social and economic autonomy, distinguishing between significant legal claims and lesser matters where their testimony is deemed reliable. It highlights the nuanced approach of the Ahl al-Bayt in adapting legal principles to the specific socio-legal status of individuals within the early Islamic community.
